profiles.meeting_scenario: A university library is planning a campus-wide rollout and promotion plan for institutional access to The Encyclopedia of Applied Linguistics, which the library has just licensed in both online and print formats. The meeting is between the library's digital resources lead and the linguistics department's undergraduate program coordinator to align on launch activities before the start of the fall term. The agenda is to decide what the 'launch package' should include, how the encyclopedia will be introduced to students and instructors, who will prepare supporting materials, and what timeline to work toward. The expected outcome is a shared plan for a September launch covering communications, instructional support, and ownership of follow-up tasks.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Electronic resource onboarding, discovery systems, vendor metadata, and instructional outreach for database adoption
members.background: Elena manages new academic database launches for the university library and regularly coordinates with faculty on integrating reference resources into teaching and research workflows.
members.private_state: Elena wants a smooth, low-risk launch that fits existing library processes and avoids promising customized academic support her small team cannot sustain during semester start-up.
hidden_assumptions: A 'launch' is complete once access, catalog discovery, the libguide page, and a general announcement are live.
A 'student-facing guide' means a short library-created webpage or PDF that explains access, search features, and citation basics, not course-specific teaching material.
When faculty say they will 'share it with instructors,' that usually means forwarding a departmental note to teaching staff rather than embedding the resource into every section.
If something is needed 'before classes start,' the practical interpretation is by local business hours on the Friday before the first week of term.
Usage review after launch normally means checking aggregate COUNTER-style platform data after the first month, not collecting qualitative feedback from individual classes.

members.name: Marcus Bell
members.role: Undergraduate Program Coordinator in Applied Linguistics
members.expertise: Curriculum coordination, first-year student support, instructor onboarding, and academic skills programming
members.background: Marcus oversees introductory course logistics, communicates with sessional instructors and TAs, and often translates department priorities into practical student support materials.
members.private_state: Marcus wants the encyclopedia to become visibly embedded in teaching from the first week so the department can show students it offers modern, research-oriented support resources.
hidden_assumptions: A 'launch' means students and instructors can immediately use the encyclopedia in real coursework through orientation, sample activities, and references in introductory classes.
A 'student-facing guide' means a polished handout or slide set with discipline-specific examples showing how students in applied linguistics should use entries for assignments.
If the library says it will handle the 'instructor outreach,' that includes making sure all intro-course conveners receive usable classroom-ready material, not just an announcement email.
Before classes start' means ready by the weekend before orientation events, because instructors and peer mentors need materials in hand before Monday.
A 'usage check-in' should include signals from actual teaching contexts, such as whether first-year seminars and writing support sessions are actively using the encyclopedia.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the launch package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly refer to getting the 'launch package' ready for September.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the operational launch package: activated access, discovery records, a libguide entry, a campus news item, and maybe a brief webinar listing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means a broader teaching launch package: student handout, instructor-ready slides, orientation mention, and examples tied to first-year assignments in addition to access.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see launch planning as routine and use the same umbrella phrase naturally; each assumes the other includes the obvious pieces from their own professional domain, so the difference feels too basic to spell out.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that a 'student-facing guide' should be prepared.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a concise library guide focused on how to log in, browse the 27 subject areas, use search and cross-references, and cite entries.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means a discipline-specific learning aid with examples such as how to use an encyclopedia entry to frame a literature review topic in Intro to Applied Linguistics.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds self-explanatory and mutually beneficial; because both versions are plausibly student-facing, the term creates false consensus rather than triggering clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: Who is included in instructor outreach
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the resource should be 'shared with instructors' before term begins.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena will consider this done if a departmental email is sent to course coordinators and the resource appears in the library newsletter for faculty.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus will consider this done only if sessional instructors and TAs for the large introductory courses receive concrete materials they can directly use in class or LMS pages.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both endorse the same goal of instructor outreach, but their completion criteria differ silently; each assumes the other applies the normal standard for academic communications in their own setting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They set several tasks to be finished 'before classes start.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena presupposes this means by Friday 5 p.m. local time before the first teaching week, which is the library's standard deadline for launch work.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus presupposes this means available by the preceding weekend so peer mentors and instructors can use materials during Sunday orientation prep and Monday-morning sessions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The academic calendar gives both a strong sense of shared context, so neither expects the phrase to be ambiguous; the discrepancy is only a few days and sounds too minor to warrant explicit scheduling talk.

turns.inner_thought: We finally have the license in place for both formats, so this should be a straightforward rollout if I keep it within normal library scope. For me, the launch package is the operational set: turn on access, make sure discovery and catalog records are clean, add the libguide entry, and push a general announcement. I want this meeting to confirm those pieces without drifting into bespoke instructional commitments my team cannot support at semester start.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Marcus. We’ve now got The Encyclopedia of Applied Linguistics licensed in both print and online, so I thought today we could pin down the September launch package and make sure we’re aligned on what needs to be in place.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect timing. If we do this well, we can make the encyclopedia feel like part of the first-year experience right away, not just another thing students discover later. When Elena says launch package, I’m assuming that means the materials instructors and students can actually use in orientation and the first week, alongside the access itself.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. The timing is really good on our side too, because we’d love to feature it pretty prominently for new students. It would be great if the launch package could support early teaching use as well.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds compatible enough. I can comfortably own the standard launch work: activate the platform, confirm catalog and discovery exposure, put up a libguide page, and draft a short news-style announcement. Adding a student-facing guide also makes sense, as long as it's the usual concise library explainer on access, searching, and citation basics.
turns.utterance: From the library side, I can take care of access activation, the catalog and discovery updates, a libguide page, and a short announcement. I’d also suggest we include a student-facing guide so there’s something clear and usable from day one.

turns.inner_thought: Great, she’s already thinking about a student-facing guide. If that guide shows students how this resource connects to the kinds of introductory assignments they actually get, it could make a real difference in whether instructors bother to use it. I assume that’s what she has in mind when she says student-facing.
turns.utterance: Yes, definitely. A student-facing guide would be especially helpful if students can immediately see how to use it for introductory assignments and for topic exploration early on.

turns.inner_thought: That all sounds fine at a high level. Once the guide and announcement are done, the normal next step is straightforward faculty communication: send the text through the department’s usual channels and include it in our faculty-facing outreach. And if we say before classes start, that means I need everything ready by Friday at business close, which is realistic.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. Once the guide and announcement are ready, we can share it with instructors through the usual channels before classes start.

turns.inner_thought: Good, so the library will handle instructor outreach. If the materials are ready to use, I can make sure all the intro teaching teams and support staff can pick them up quickly. Sharing it with instructors only works if there’s something they can drop right into course spaces without having to build from scratch, and before classes start means they need it in hand before the weekend prep window.
turns.utterance: Great. And having something instructors can drop straight into first-year course sites will make sharing it with instructors much easier before classes start.

turns.inner_thought: He seems happy with the timeline, which is reassuring. I can draft the guide and the outreach copy by the Friday before term, and that should be sufficient for the launch package as I understand it. I’m not hearing any need for anything beyond the standard pieces, which is a relief.
turns.utterance: I can draft the guide and the outreach copy by the Friday before term, and I’d expect that to keep everything on track for the launch.

turns.inner_thought: Friday is tight, but if that means the materials are effectively done and available, I can still route them to orientation leaders and intro teaching teams for their weekend prep. They’ll need to be able to use what comes over without much reworking. I’m assuming Friday delivery still supports that before-classes-start window we’re all imagining.
turns.utterance: Friday sounds good. I can make sure orientation leaders and the intro teaching teams have the materials when they’re prepping over the weekend.

turns.inner_thought: Once it’s live, I’d like a light-touch follow-up rather than anything labor-intensive. A usage review after a few weeks should just mean checking the platform data to see whether people are finding it. That gives us enough signal without creating a whole assessment project.
turns.utterance: Then maybe a few weeks after launch we do a light check-in on usage, just to see whether it seems to be landing well.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, and I’d want that check-in to tell us whether it’s really showing up in teaching contexts, not just whether someone clicked into it. If first-year seminars, writing support, and teaching staff are actually using it, that’s the sign the rollout worked. I assume Elena includes that kind of real-world uptake in a usage check-in.
turns.utterance: I like that. It’ll be useful to hear how students and teaching staff are actually using it in those early-semester settings.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we have a clean division of labor. I’ll produce the library pieces: the guide, the discovery setup, and the outreach text. Marcus can circulate it through his department contacts, which should satisfy the plan to share it with instructors. This keeps expectations manageable and within process.
turns.utterance: Perfect. So I’ll prepare the guide, activate the discovery side, and send over the outreach text, and then you can circulate it through the department.

turns.inner_thought: That should work well. Once the launch package is out, we ought to have what we need for instructors and students to encounter the encyclopedia right away in a visible way. I’m assuming the materials Elena sends will be ready enough for teaching teams to use directly.
turns.utterance: That sounds great. Once the launch package is out, I think the encyclopedia should have a strong start with both instructors and students.
